title.en: Edinburgh Audio Tour: Underground Echoes and City Secrets

events.description: Beneath the cobblestones of the Royal Mile, the cries of rebellion, sermons, and secret agreements still echo. Edinburgh stands proud, but the city hides a darker and stranger layer.

A spire pierces the Edinburgh sky, blackened by centuries of secrets and storms. The city below shudders with history both whispered and shouted. Uncover a side of Edinburgh most never see on this self-guided audio tour. Move from the looming Scott Monument to the timeworn stones of Greyfriars Kirk, through the halls of New College and beyond, chasing the tales that haunt every step. Why did a silent midnight duel near the kirk change the fate of a nation? Which monument conceals the scars of a forgotten rebellion? What odd ritual once echoed through New College's secluded courtyards? Wander ancient closes and grand crescents. Trace the city's shadows and scandals in corners tourists rush past. Every moment here tilts between awe and revelation, promising fresh eyes on a living legend. Take the first step into Edinburgh's tangled heart and let its true story unfold.

title.en: Dr Arnott's Sampling Sensation - Immersive Workshop & Guided Tour

events.description: Delve into the strange and surprisingly scientific world of 17th-century medicine at The Real Mary King’s Close. This immersive experience uncovers the practices of Dr Arnott, one of the Close’s wealthiest and most intriguing former residents. A trained physician with a taste for the unconventional, Dr Arnott diagnosed his patients by examining their urine for colour, smell… and even taste. Now, it’s your turn to step into his shoes. Begin with a 1-hour guided tour through Edinburgh’s hidden underground streets, before joining a hands-on workshop where you’ll put your senses to the test. Analyse samples, follow Dr Arnott’s methods, and create your own herbal remedy in this interactive and entertaining experience. It’s historical, it’s hands-on, and yes… it’s a little bit pee-culiar. Includes: - 1-hour guided tour - 30-minute interactive workshop - 1 hot drink Good to know: - Suitable for ages 5+ (no under 5s) - Audio guides available for the tour (not the workshop) - Tickets are non-transferable and non-changeable

A Halloween ghost tour of Edinburgh’s shadowy closes and vaults with a glass of witches’ brew to finish. Explore Edinburgh’s Old Town and vaults before settling into the candlelit Megget’s Cellar for a complimentary drink. Walk with spirits and drink with the dead this Halloween. Tradition has it that Samhuinn, or Halloween, is the time when the veil between worlds lifts, and the spirits of the dead drift among the living. It is the perfect time to visit one of Scotland's most haunted sites. Step into the spirit of Halloween on a spine-tingling ghost tour through Edinburgh’s medieval streets and haunted underground vaults. Hear tales of the city’s past residents and stories of spirits stepping through the veil between worlds. Follow chilling tales through the shadows before ending the night with a reviving Halloween cocktail. Descend into the spirit world Your Master Storyteller will guide you along cobbled streets, once steeped in blood, guts and gore, echoing with the sounds of the city’s grisly past. They might even teach you a centuries-old tradition or two to protect yourself on Samhuinn, a time when spirits enter this realm. You’ll then descend into the famous vaults — a flickering maze of candlelit chambers that are certain to maintain a ghost or two within their ancient walls. Finally, still your nerves with a glass of witches’ brew in our underground Megget’s Cellar as your Storyteller weaves more tales by candlelight.

events.description: Edinburgh synth-pop duo Both Hands celebrate the release of their debut album Be Like A Mountain In A Moonlit Way with a very special afternoon of live music, performance, and visuals at Fruitmarket Warehouse. Released via Lost Map Records, the album brings together Hailey Beavis's distinctive vocals and confessional lyrics with Brian Pokora's dreamy, wonky electronic production, creating a strange, joyful and beautiful world somewhere between synth-pop, trip-hop and experimental electronic music. For the launch, Both Hands will bring that world to life in a specially created live show, alongside Accident Machine, Thundermoon and Supper Club DJs. Expect big synths, infectious electronic pop, unusual sounds, homemade visual magic, performance and plenty of dancing in the wonderful warehouse space at Fruitmarket. And bring the kids! This is a daytime, all-ages album launch, designed to be enjoyed by grown-ups and little ones alike. Children are very welcome to come along and experience the music, dancing and visual world of Both Hands. Children aged 5 and under go free, with tickets for children over 5 available for £5. title.en: Flamenco Night Party - Flamenco Tablao · Tuflamenco

events.description: TuFlamenco returns with a true flamenco tablao — raw, powerful, and uncompromising. No fusion, no narrative, no distractions. Just pure flamenco: cante, guitar and dance in their most direct and authentic form. This is flamenco as it is lived — close, intense and spontaneous. The deep voices of flamenco singing, the precision and fire of the guitar, and the strength, elegance and risk of live flamenco dance come together in an intimate setting where compás leads and emotion rules. After the great success of our May edition, we are delighted to return once again to The Voodoo Rooms with a new night of authentic flamenco — and a few special surprises prepared for this occasion. A 5 star tablao experience, praised year after year and recognised as a benchmark for flamenco in Scotland and across the UK. Whether you are a seasoned aficionado or discovering flamenco for the first time, this night promises truth, artistry and unforgettable energy. Approx. 80-minute performance Confirmed Artists - Inma Montero & Danielo Olivera – Flamenco singing & compás - Daniel Martínez – Flamenco guitar - Gabriela Pouso, Jara Pérez – Flamenco dance Don’t hear about it from others — come and live flamenco for real.

Their releases have included numerous singles and four albums on various labels, including Cherry Red and Radar, as well as recording four Peel sessions. The band has received critical acclaim, including singles of the week on the Radio 1 evening session and NME. They have also toured and shared bills with a diverse array of bands, including Stereolab, Sebadoh, Arab Strap and Sonic Youth. Pavement’s Stephen Malkmus described Prolapse as the best band of the weekend at Reading Festival. After a long hiatus, the band reformed in 2015 and occasionally play live dates. This short UK tour offers a rare chance to experience the Prolapse live show. title.en: Exhibition: A Drunk Man Looks at the Thistle

events.description: This exhibition by painter Alexander Moffat marks the centenary of Hugh MacDiarmid’s visionary poem A Drunk Man Looks at the Thistle. First published in 1926, 2026 marks the centenary of the poem, an epic work written in MacDiarmid’s synthetic Scots that would prove a landmark in the story of modern Scottish literature. Alexander Moffat’s paintings range from 1978 when he made drawings of the poet in his home at Brownsbank Cottage near Biggar and continue into the present with paintings of MacDiarmid and his close colleagues from the Borders, William Johnstone and Francis George Scott. The three ‘Border Guards’ launched the Scottish Renaissance of the early 1920s and beyond. F G Scott was not only MacDiarmid’s schoolteacher in Langholm, he was the originator of the idea of a drunk man looking at a thistle and assisted with the editing and final structure of the poem. Born in Dunfermline, Moffat studied at Edinburgh College of Art from 1960 to 64. Alongside his friend John Bellany, Moffat emerged as one of the Scottish Realists, so-called because of their social awareness and rejection of the decorative principles that defined much Scottish art during the first half of the 20th century. Moffat was particularly close to the poet Hugh MacDiarmid and his literary circle. From 1979 Moffat taught at Glasgow School of Art where he encouraged a new generation of Scottish figurative painters including Peter Howson, Ken Currie and Steven Campbell. events.description: Big Country: 'The Seer' 40th Anniversary Tour Celebrate 40 years of a Scottish masterpiece live at Edinburgh's premier underground venue! In 1986, Dunfermline's alt-rock icons Big Country released their seminal third studio album, The Seer. Boasting towering tracks like "Look Away", "The Teacher", and the sweeping title track, the album cemented their signature widescreen, bagpipe-inflected guitar sound in rock history. To honor this milestone, Big Country - led by co-founder and longest-serving member Bruce Watson - are heading out on a massive UK anniversary run. They land at The Liquid Room in Edinburgh on Sunday, 20th December 2026 for a monumental, high-energy performance of tracks from The Seer alongside their timeless greatest hits like "In A Big Country" and "Fields Of Fire". Special Guest: Evan Peters Presents The Alarm Adding to this historic tour, the band will be joined by very special guests Evan Peters Presents The Alarm. This run honors an emotional pact made between Bruce Watson and Mike Peters following Mike's cancer diagnosis, celebrating the triumphant survival, bond, and timeless hits of both bands live on one stage.

events.description: RUTS DC present 50 years of RUTS Music (1977-2027) THE RUTS + special guests In 1977, The Ruts emerged from London with a sound unlike anybody else around them - the raw urgency of punk colliding with reggae, dub and rock, driven by formidable musicianship and a fierce sense of purpose. With Malcolm Owen, Paul Fox, Dave Ruffy and Segs Jennings, The Ruts created a body of music whose power has endured far beyond its original moment. After losing Malcolm Owen in 1980, the remaining members chose integrity over nostalgia by re-inventing themselves as Ruts DC, eventually losing Paul Fox in 2007. Ruts DC remain a living, evolving band to this day. But the time has come to celebrate the whole story. This tour is about taking the music that exploded out of a movement and bringing it onto a stage in 2027 with all its urgency and relevance intact. events.description: The Too Bad Jims got their name from the seminal Fat Possum album "Too Bad Jim" by the hugely influential blues musician RL Burnside. The band plays a gritty high-octane mix of North Mississippi Hill Country blues and boogie. It all initially started as a casual collaboration between two veteran and multiple award-winning musicians, Little Victor and Son Jack Jr. and they shortly after rounded out the trio with the one and only Nick Simonon (Brother of Paul Simonon of The Clash) on drums and things really started cookin’! Their unique and unusual combination of dual rough and ready vocals, bare-bones electric guitars, slashing bottleneck, and a heavily rhythm-oriented groove, delivers a hypnotic, raw, and earthy sound typical of a North Mississippi juke joint. After relocating to the London area from Seattle, Washington USA, Son Jack Jr (an avid long-time player of this style of blues) got in touch with Little Victor Mac whom he had befriended on social media since Victor's glory days with Louisiana Red in the late 2000s The two men never met in person until a couple of years ago but ever since their first jam, they sounded like they’d been playing together since day one. Little Victor (who moved to England a little before Son Jack Jr.) has deep knowledge of this style of music, particularly RL Burnside.
